newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: U.S. official visits Sri Lanka's troubled north.
newsitem.headline: U.S. official visits Sri Lanka's troubled north.

text.p: U.S. Assistant Secretary of State Robin Raphel visited Sri Lanka's troubled northern region on Friday to meet international aid agencies helping Tamil refugees displaced in the country's 14-year civil war.

U.S. embassy and Sri Lankan foreign ministry officials said Raphel met officials of the United Nations High Commission on Refugees and the International Committee of the Red Cross in Vavuniya, 220 km (140 miles) north of Colombo.
U.S. embassy and aid agency officials declined to comment on Raphel's discussions in Vavuniya.

Vavuniya is the transit point for Tamils fleeing the war between the Sri Lankan military and the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Ealam (LTTE), who are fighting for a separate Tamil homeland in the north and east.

About 600,000 Tamils have been displaced since October 1995 when government forces captured Jaffna peninsula, the main LTTE stronghold in the north. The government says the 14-year old war has killed 50,000 people but the LTTE says the toll is much higher.
A senior U.S. embassy official said Raphel's visit was a routine one.
Raphel, the U.S. State Department's chief of South Asian affairs, has already visited Pakistan and Bangladesh and will visit India starting Saturday.
